title: Skull Bumps, Rat Mazes, and Brain Networks: Phrenology, Lashley's Cortical Equipotentiality, and Functional Connectomics on Trial — Two centuries of brain localization extremes: Gall's cranioscopy & Lashley's 30-year rat-maze equipotentiality laws vs. Scoville & Milner's Patient H.M. hippocampal amnesia, Kanwisher's millimeter-specialized FFA, Haxby's distributed ventral-temporal MVPA vectors, Poldrack's Bayesian demolition of fMRI 'neo-phrenology' & Boes/Fox's 1,000-subject human connectome lesion-network mapping; parallel-cue redundancy & BrainMap Bayes-factor math plus spotting blobology in disguise

teenKit.tldr: For two centuries, brain science bounced wildly between two false extremes: that every tiny personality trait sits in a specific skull bump, or that the brain is just an undifferentiated sponge. Modern connectomics proves the truth is a complex, wired network.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how your brain is actually organized protects you from falling for modern pseudoscience, bad AI hype, and "neo-phrenology" marketing tricks.
keyTakeaways: Franz Joseph Gall's phrenology tried to map complex moral traits onto literal bumps on the skull, treating the brain like a 27-part postal code.
Karl Lashley spent decades cutting out rat brain tissue and concluded that memory has no specific address, arguing the brain is totally flexible and uniform (equipotentiality).

Modern brain science uses functional connectomics to show that while specific regions exist, higher cognitive functions rely on distributed, wired networks rather than isolated boxes or giant sponges.

vocab.meaning: A thoroughly debunked 19th-century pseudo-science claiming a person's psychological traits and mental faculties can be measured by reading the physical bumps on their skull.
Karl Lashley's discredited theory that any part of the cerebral cortex can take over the job of any other part, meaning only the total amount of brain tissue matters, not where damage happens.
A millimeter-specialized region in the human brain that lights up specifically when you look at faces.
The modern mapping approach that treats the brain not as isolated islands or a single uniform sponge, but as an intricately wired, multi-region communication network.

quiz.question: What was the core claim of Franz Joseph Gall's 19th-century phrenology?
options: Mental faculties and moral traits are localized in specific brain regions and create visible bumps on the skull.
The brain acts entirely as a single uniform sponge where any part can handle any task.
Memories are stored exclusively inside the hippocampus through electrical loops.
Brain functions cannot be localized because the skull completely blocks all neural signals.
quiz.explanation: Gall believed the brain was parceled out into isolated organs for traits like "amativeness" or "veneration" that pushed outward on the skull bones.

quiz.question: How did Karl Lashley attempt to prove his theory of equipotentiality using rats?
options: By mapping their electrical impulses while they slept.
By systematically ablating (cutting or burning away) varying amounts of their neocortex and testing their maze-running memory.
By breeding rats with unusually large skull bumps to see if they learned faster.
By scanning their brains using high-resolution functional MRI machines.
quiz.explanation: Lashley spent decades removing chunks of rat cortex and concluded that memory loss depended only on how much tissue was destroyed, not where.

quiz.question: What major modern insight finally bridged the historical gap between strict localization and total holism?
options: Proving that skull bumps actually do indicate high intelligence.
Discovering that rats have completely different brain structures than humans.
Mapping the brain as an interconnected functional network where specialized regions collaborate dynamically.
Showing that brain cells never change their specialized jobs under any circumstances.
quiz.explanation: Functional connectomics revealed that the brain uses specialized nodes working together in distributed networks rather than isolated boxes or undifferentiated mush.
